subject.title: Support session-level environment variables for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-spawn `sessions_spawn.env` for ACP sessions, or keep ACP environment injection limited to configured/trusted surfaces such as a future per-agent env contract?
rationale: The request is useful and upstream ACPX can carry session env, but it creates a model-callable credential-to-host-subprocess boundary, so automation should not choose the trust model, allowed keys, redaction, or reuse semantics.

options.title: Design a safe per-spawn env contract
options.body: Approve `sessions_spawn.env` only with validation, redaction, blocked-key or SecretRef-style handling, session freshness semantics, and focused tests across tool, manager, and ACPX paths.

options.title: Route to configured agent env
options.body: Keep this issue open or later close it as superseded only if maintainers decide a configured `agents.list[].env` path is the supported solution for these use cases.

options.title: Reject per-spawn env
options.body: Close the request if maintainers decide model-callable ACP environment injection is too broad for OpenClaw's security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design a safe per-spawn env contract
recommendation.body: Approve `sessions_spawn.env` only with validation, redaction, blocked-key or SecretRef-style handling, session freshness semantics, and focused tests across tool, manager, and ACPX paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACPX runtime work and adjacent per-agent-env review context make this the best available owner for the product/security choice.
